notes.b1/j1/B-r1: Lines are 4-7-4 (midwinter dusk = 4, a thin veil above the ridge = 7, turns pearl, then gray = 4), so not 5-7-5 but a deliberate short-long-short with the em dash; the veil turning pearl then gray evokes nacreous clouds at twilight accurately and gives a fading turn.
notes.b1/j1/A-r1: Exact 5-7-5 (Nacreous glow spreads = 5, across the winter dusk sky = 7, clouds no one expects = 5) and names the right phenomenon, but the glow is abstract and 'no one expects' is a stock phrase that ends flat.
notes.b1/j1/B-r2: Exact 5-7-5 (Late in autumn wind = 5, a lens above the ridge stands = 7, while the air runs through = 5); the lenticular cloud is accurately evoked as a stationary lens over a ridge in moving air, and that stillness-in-motion is a real turn, though the opener 'Late in autumn wind' is clumsy.
notes.b1/j1/A-r2: Exact 5-7-5 (Pearl-lit, high, unseen = 5, nacreous clouds bloom at dusk = 7, winter's rarest sky = 5); names nacreous accurately and 'bloom' is vivid, but 'rarest' just restates the prompt and 'unseen' stays abstract.
notes.b1/j2/B-r2: Syllables 5-7-5 (Late in autumn wind / a lens above the ridge stands / while the air runs through); a lenticular cloud drawn as a stationary lens while air streams past is an accurate, unnamed evocation, with a clean turn from wind to stillness.
notes.b1/j2/A-r2: Syllables 5-7-5 (Pearl-lit, high, unseen / na-cre-ous clouds bloom at dusk / winter's rarest sky); it names nacreous clouds accurately for altitude and dusk timing, but 'winter's rarest sky' is a stock closing phrase and the poem does not turn.
notes.b1/j2/A-r1: Syllables 5-7-5 (Na-cre-ous glow spreads / across the winter dusk sky / clouds no one expects); the nacreous naming and dusk glow are accurate, but 'clouds no one expects' is a generic turn and the glow is less seen than the other entries.
notes.b1/j2/B-r1: Syllables 4-7-4 (midwinter dusk / a thin veil above the ridge / turns pearl, then gray), a deliberate short-long-short shape that falls one syllable short per outer line; the veil fading from pearl to gray is a true nacreous behavior and gives the strongest feeling of change.
notes.b1/j3/A-r2: Exact 5-7-5 (Pearl-lit, high, unseen = 5; nacreous clouds bloom at dusk = 7; winter's rarest sky = 5) with an accurate nacreous/polar-stratospheric evocation, but "unseen" and "winter's rarest sky" are stock phrasing that tells the rarity instead of showing it.
notes.b1/j3/B-r2: Exact 5-7-5 (Late in autumn wind = 5; a lens above the ridge stands = 7; while the air runs through = 5) and a lenticular cloud that holds still while the wind passes through it, which is the real physics and a quietly strong turn.

notes.b2/j1/B-r3: Syllables are 5-7-5 (First snow on the ridge / the lens holds, wind running through / and the cloud stays still), and the lens cloud is an accurate lenticular evocation, though it is never named; the stillness-against-wind turn is quiet and effective.
